evidenceScope: These sources describe methods, not evidence that this app can diagnose conditions or establish causes.
longHorizon: 14–28 days is an exploratory horizon. The trend assumes its current slope continues; the multiple-input model fits the selected horizon directly. Longer horizons leave fewer training pairs and can miss changes in routine. Check later-data errors for that horizon; a narrow interval alone is not evidence of accuracy.
validationChart: Predictions compared with held-out observations and 95% predictive intervals
validationLegend: Points: later observations. Line: predictions from the training model. Band: 95% predictive interval. These observations were not used to fit that model.
scoreExplanation: The interval score combines width with a penalty when an observation falls outside the 95% interval: width + 40 × distance beyond the nearest bound. Averaged over held-out dates, in outcome units. Compare only the same outcome, dates and horizon; widening every interval does not guarantee a better score.
biasExplanation: A positive mean error means underprediction; a negative value means overprediction. Opposing errors can cancel, so read this alongside MAE.
bayesCitation: Murphy, K. P. (2007). Conjugate Bayesian analysis of the Gaussian distribution.
bootstrapCitation: Politis, D. N. & Romano, J. P. (1992). A Circular Block-Resampling Procedure for Stationary Data.
intervalCitation: Gneiting, T. & Raftery, A. E. (2007). Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation. JASA 102(477), 359–378.
